title: Design squash-merge landing for a chain of verified jobs
summary: Write a design (doc plus decision entry, no code) for how the landing/history gate can accept a squash merge of a chain of sequentially verified jobs, so adopters needn't restrict to one job per commit. It builds on D66–D68 and design §7.3, and recommends one option from the alternatives.

defaults_applied.how: Write the design with alternatives before any gate code is built; implementation is a follow-up.
Cite invariant.rs lines, design §7.3, D66-D68; label unrun claims as inferred.
One design doc plus one decision entry and a changelog line; no code.
Design states how the rule would be enforced by the gate rather than by prose.
Doc written for an outside reader with the problem restated.

assumptions: 'Design' means a written design with alternatives and a decision entry (the 'designed' default), not an implementation of the gate change.
The goal is that adopters can squash-merge a PR holding a chain of verified jobs and the history/landing check passes without per-commit exemptions.
The chain is sequential: each job is based on the previous job's landed or candidate state.
Existing decisions D60-D68 stay in force; the design proposes and does not supersede them until accepted.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new design document under docs/design/ (e.g. squash-chain-landing.md) states the problem: a squash of a chain of verified jobs yields one commit adding several jobs' closing records, which `landing` in crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs refuses (more than one closing job; whole-tree fingerprint mismatch), citing D66 and design §7.3.

The design lists at least three alternatives (e.g. per-job patch composition proof, chain-aware landing rule where only the final job's fingerprint must equal the landed tree and earlier jobs must be ancestors by recorded base, restricting merge methods, exemption) with tradeoffs, and recommends one with reasons.

The recommended design specifies what records link a chain (e.g. each job's base tree/fingerprint equals the prior job's verified candidate fingerprint), the exact check the gate would perform on a squash, how it fails (refusal messages), and how it keeps the 'nothing reaches main unverified' and prediction-precedes-outcome (M23) properties.

docs/decisions.md gains a new entry (next number after D68) in the existing format (Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal, Provenance) recording the design as proposed, with claims labeled as read from code or inferred, and no implementation claimed.

The design names the follow-up implementation work (gate change in invariant.rs, tests in landing_tests.rs, update of design §7.3 and docs/enforcement.md) and states that this change modifies no Rust code, athena.toml, workflows, or other governance files.
CHANGELOG.md has a line noting the design; no records/ or governance files change.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy`: all still pass, and `git diff --stat` shows only files under docs/ and CHANGELOG.md.

out_of_scope: Implementing the gate change in crates/athena-gate
Changing athena.toml, workflows, or the [history] exempt list
Rewriting main or splitting commit ee4b0dd
Configuring repository merge-method settings on the host
departures: Doc-only design work should cost slightly less than the reference; verification is lighter but acceptance of the chosen design is uncertain, so intervention stays near reference.
